pages.title: Overview
pages.scope: What the project is, its main parts and how they fit, and where to read next.

pages.title: System Architecture
pages.scope: Explain how declarative pipelines, the shared incremental engine, persistence, connectors, and the Python and Rust interfaces fit together. Direct readers to detailed subsystem pages.

pages.title: Declarative Processing Model
pages.scope: Trace a source-to-target pipeline through an app, processing components, stable paths, memoized functions, and declared target states; explain how these concepts enable incremental updates and cleanup.

pages.title: Shared Engine and Language Boundaries
pages.scope: Explain EngineProfile and trace how the Python extension and native Rust SDK adapt host contexts, processors, persisted values, target handlers, and action sinks to the shared engine.

pages.title: Native Rust SDK
pages.scope: Explain the Rust SDK's public API, Ctx-based pipeline programming, procedural macros, feature gates, and direct integration with the core engine.

pages.title: Incremental Execution
pages.scope: Trace an app update through root and child component execution, prior-state reuse, and live processing; link to the detailed mechanisms.

pages.title: App Execution and CLI
pages.scope: Cover app construction and loading, update options, previews, drops, and operation handles across Python, CLI, and Rust.

pages.title: Component Mounting and Identity
pages.scope: Explain foreground and background mounts, readiness, keyed fan-out, and stable paths that identify child components.

pages.title: Processing Functions
pages.scope: Explain decorated Python functions, sync and async execution, bound methods, and processor adapters, with the corresponding Rust function interface.

pages.title: Memoization and State Reuse
pages.scope: Explain component and function memoization, input keys, tracked state validation, dependency reuse, and restoration of cached declarations.

pages.title: Logic Change Detection
pages.scope: Explain logic fingerprints, versions and declared dependencies, registry validation, and propagation of changes to callers.

pages.title: Live Component Lifecycle
pages.scope: Describe catch-up and live modes, readiness, keyed and full updates, periodic refresh, cancellation, and shutdown.

pages.title: Live Maps and Change Feeds
pages.scope: Explain feed and view interfaces, snapshot and subscription ordering, keyed change delivery, and in-memory LiveMap ownership and watch behavior.

pages.title: Target Reconciliation
pages.scope: Explain how component declarations become reconciled external actions, tracking records, and committed ownership; connect the stages and their failure boundaries.

pages.title: Target Declarations and Hierarchies
pages.scope: Explain root providers, stable keyed target states, child providers, attachments, provider generations, and child invalidation.

pages.title: Ownership, Submission, and Cleanup
pages.scope: Trace precommit reads and claims, action application, commit ordering, ownership transfer, tombstones, and cleanup of disappeared components and declarations.

pages.title: Custom Target Handlers and Sinks
pages.scope: Explain the handler and sink contracts, tracking records, child handler factories, retry-safe reconciliation, idempotent actions, shared batching, and failure isolation.

pages.title: State Diffs and Schema Evolution
pages.scope: Explain tracking record transitions, managed ownership policies, composite diffs, schema comparisons, and how destructive or lossy transitions affect child state.

pages.title: Source and Target Connectors
pages.scope: Map built-in integrations by source and target roles, supported live feeds, language availability, and shared connector helpers.

pages.title: Filesystem and File Resources
pages.scope: Explain file paths, metadata and content fingerprints, path matching, directory traversal, live watching, and filesystem target reconciliation in Python and Rust.

pages.title: Cloud File Sources
pages.scope: Compare object storage and Google Drive enumeration, file identity, metadata and content access, including OCI's optional event-driven live view.

pages.title: Relational Database Connectors
pages.scope: Compare PostgreSQL, SQLite and Doris source and target capabilities, table schemas, row synchronization and indexes; link to connector-specific details.

pages.title: PostgreSQL Source and Target
pages.scope: Trace repeatable-read source enumeration and keyed rows, then PostgreSQL table, row and index reconciliation in the Python and Rust connectors.

pages.title: SQLite and Doris Targets
pages.scope: Explain table and row synchronization, schema changes, and vector and other index management in SQLite and Doris.

pages.title: Warehouse Connectors
pages.scope: Compare BigQuery and Snowflake table schema reconciliation, value encoding, row upserts and deletes.

pages.title: Vector and Key-Value Targets
pages.scope: Compare target containers, vector schemas, indexes and record models across LanceDB, zvec, Qdrant, Turbopuffer and Valkey; direct readers to implementation details.

pages.title: LanceDB and zvec Targets
pages.scope: Explain embedded table and collection schemas, vector and full-text indexes, and row or document synchronization.

pages.title: Qdrant, Turbopuffer and Valkey Targets
pages.scope: Explain collection, namespace and index management, vector definitions, and point, row and document synchronization.

pages.title: Graph Database Targets
pages.scope: Compare graph connections, table and relation targets, record ownership and vector indexes across Neo4j, FalkorDB and SurrealDB.

pages.title: Neo4j and FalkorDB Targets
pages.scope: Explain node and relationship declarations, Cypher action ordering, schema and vector index management, including the Rust SDK's shared Cypher graph implementation.

pages.title: SurrealDB Target
pages.scope: Explain record and relation targets, field ownership, table schema, action ordering and vector indexes.

pages.title: Streaming Connectors
pages.scope: Explain Kafka and Iggy streams and keyed maps, catch-up boundaries, ordered offset acknowledgment, single-watcher behavior and message targets.

pages.title: Transformation and Intelligence
pages.scope: Overview of composable operations for splitting, code analysis, embeddings, model calls, and entity resolution in Python and Rust.

pages.title: Text Splitting and Provenance
pages.scope: Explain separator and recursive splitting, language-aware boundaries, overlap, fallback behavior, and position-tracked chunks.

pages.title: Code Parsing and Context Views
pages.scope: Explain reusable parsed sources, language registration, semantic elements, syntax-aware splitting, and source-grounded context views.

pages.title: Structural Matching and Prefilters
pages.scope: Explain pattern compilation, metavariables and captures, language-specific matching, prefilters, and index terms.

pages.title: Embedding Models and Vector Types
pages.scope: Explain embedder interfaces, local text and image embedding, vector schema metadata, and embedding workflows.

pages.title: Model Calls and Multimodal Processing
pages.scope: Describe LiteLLM and Rust HTTP integrations for hosted embeddings, transcription, and JSON chat, alongside model-call and image-processing examples.

pages.title: Entity Resolution
pages.scope: Explain embedding-based candidate selection, pair resolvers, canonical policies, component partitioning, and resolution events in Python and Rust.

pages.title: Runtime and Shared Mechanisms
pages.scope: Orient readers to environments, shared execution resources, persistent state, and operational visibility across the Python and Rust APIs.

pages.title: Context, Resources, and Identity
pages.scope: Explain typed context providers, tracked resource dependencies, component context propagation, and thread attachment. Introduce stable ID generation and link to its detailed page.

pages.title: Stable ID Generation
pages.scope: Explain memoized IDs and UUIDs, generators for repeated dependencies, occurrence ordinals, and batched allocation by the core ID sequencer.

pages.title: Environment Configuration and Lifecycle
pages.scope: Explain settings and environment variables, lifespan-managed resources, default and explicit environments, event loops, runtime startup, and shutdown.

pages.title: Persistent State and User State
pages.scope: Describe LMDB app stores, persisted component and target records, memo values, and explicit user state; link to transaction internals.

pages.title: LMDB Transactions and Write Batching
pages.scope: Explain the single-writer batcher, retryable transaction bodies, thread affinity, map resizing, and submission commit plans.

pages.title: Types, Serialization, and Fingerprints
pages.scope: Explain Python type interpretation, durable serialization and restricted unpickling, the separate compact in-memory target-state codec, and fingerprints used for change detection.

pages.title: Concurrency, Batching, and Rate Limits
pages.scope: Explain component admission and token lending, shared batch queues, function and sink batching, and rate limiting. Introduce execution runners and link to their detailed page.

pages.title: Execution Runners and GPU Pools
pages.scope: Explain Python execution runners, subprocess execution, GPU allocation and fractions, and the shared GPU pool.

pages.title: Deadlines, Cancellation, and Failures
pages.scope: Explain deadline propagation, cancellation checks, exception handler chains, transient retry classification, and failure isolation.

pages.title: Inspection, Progress, and Telemetry
pages.scope: Describe persisted-state inspection, progress and statistics handles, terminal reporting, and telemetry controls.

pages.title: Development
pages.scope: Orient contributors to the repository's build, validation, examples, documentation and release workflows.

pages.title: Local Setup and Builds
pages.scope: Set up Rust, uv and prek; build and rebuild the Python extension; select optional dependencies; and run examples against a local checkout.

pages.title: Testing and Performance
pages.scope: Explain test environments, Docker-backed fixtures, CI test matrices, Rust SDK feature checks and benchmark workflows.

pages.title: Contribution and Quality Checks
pages.scope: Cover contributor conventions, prek hooks, formatting, linting, generated artifacts and checks for core and SDK changes.

pages.title: Example Application Patterns
pages.scope: Connect runnable Python and Rust examples to retrieval, document processing, knowledge graphs and streaming pipelines.

pages.title: Packaging and Releases
pages.scope: Explain version synchronization, wheel and source distribution builds, release validation and publishing; link to runtime configuration and CLI pages for operating apps.

pages.title: Documentation Site and Agent Exports
pages.scope: Describe the Astro build, sidebar navigation, inline diagram components, generated CLI reference and machine-readable documentation routes.

pages.title: Glossary
pages.scope: Project-specific terms, each with a one-line meaning and the page that explains it.
